documentTitle: Venue Egress, Corridor Geometry & Density Reference Principles
authority: Vyuha Compiled Venue Planning Guidance (Fruin / Weidmann / Fire Egress Standards)

sections.summary: General two-way circulation corridors below 2.4 m create friction, while pinch points narrower than 1.5 m cause severe queueing and flow breakdown under moderate surge.
sections.verbatimQuote: Primary pedestrian circulation corridors should maintain at least 2.4 m clear width; passages narrower than 1.5 m create severe flow constriction and require widening, one-way control, or diversion.

sections.summary: When three or more pedestrian tributaries merge, the downstream outgoing corridor should preserve at least 75% of the combined incoming widths or distribute flows across parallel exits.
sections.verbatimQuote: At high-convergence junctions where three or more pedestrian streams merge, downstream corridor width below 75 percent of combined incoming widths induces rapid upstream shockwave compression.

sections.summary: Eliminate dead-end corridors exceeding 10 m and verify every public gathering zone connects cleanly to entry, exit, and emergency egress routes.
sections.verbatimQuote: Dead-end corridors exceeding 10 m without through-egress trap turning crowds during surges; every public zone must maintain continuous connectivity to at least one normal exit and one emergency exit.

sections.sectionTitle: Exit Gate Clearance Aprons & Discharge Sightlines
sections.summary: Maintain at least a 3.0 m unobstructed discharge apron immediately outside and inside every exit gate and emergency exit so exiting crowds can fan out without rebounding.
sections.verbatimQuote: An unobstructed discharge apron of at least 3.0 m must be maintained clear of barricades, stalls, or equipment at every exit gate and emergency exit to prevent back-pressure jamming.

sections.sectionTitle: Crowd Density Regimes & Explicit Local Assumption Review
sections.summary: Fruin/Weidmann reference studies distinguish comfortable moving flow (< 1.0 p/m2), slow dense circulation (1.5–2.0 p/m2), and critical congestion (> 2.0–4.0 p/m2); planners must cite local jurisdiction guidance and obtain safety reviewer sign-off rather than assuming a universal limit.
sections.verbatimQuote: Published crowd-flow literature notes progressive speed degradation above 1.5 persons per square meter and severe congestion risk beyond 2.0 to 3.0 persons per square meter; exact design assumptions must cite local statutory or engineering guidance and undergo professional review.

sections.sectionTitle: Blueprint Scale Verification & Perspective Distortion Check
sections.summary: Verify uploaded blueprints with a perpendicular cross-axis check segment; mismatches above 5% indicate oblique camera perspective or uneven scaling unsuitable for clearance decisions.
sections.verbatimQuote: When calibrating aerial photographs or scanned site plans, a cross-axis scale verification mismatch exceeding 5 percent indicates perspective distortion requiring re-calibration or an orthographic plan.
